question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{log}_{5}⁡(x+2) & =6 \\ {log}_{5}⁡(x+2) & =\frac{6}{3} \\ {log}_{5}⁡(x+3) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $5,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡(x+2) & =2 \\ {5}^{{log}_{5}⁡(x+2)} & ={5}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${5}^{{log}_{5}⁡(x+2)}=x+2.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & ={5}^{2} \\ x+2 & =25 \\ x & =23.\end{aligned}
$$
